etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English specialte, Old French specialte, especialte, from Latin specialitas.

definitions.definition: That in which one specializes; a chosen expertise or talent.

quote.citation: 1858, Charles Kingsley, “My Winter-Garden”, in Fraser’s Magazine‎[1], volume 57, page 410:
quote.text: Even men of boundless knowledge, like Humboldt, must have had once their speciality, their pet subject, or they would have, strictly speaking, no knowledge at all.

definitions.definition: A product that originates in and is characteristic of a place.

quote.citation: c. 1602, William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Troylus and Cressida”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene iii]:
quote.text: The specialty of rule hath been neglected:And, look, how many Grecian tents do standHollow upon this plain, so many hollow factions.

definitions.definition: An attribute or quality peculiar to a species.
(law) A contract or obligation under seal; a contract by deed; a writing, under seal, given as security for a debt particularly specified.

quote.citation: c. 1590–1592 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Taming of the Shrew”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene i]:
quote.text: Let specialties be therefore drawne betweene vs,That couenants may be kept on either hand.

quote.citation: 1812, Joseph Chitty, A Treatise on Pleading, with a Collection of Practical Precedents, and Notes Thereon, 2nd American edition, edited by Thomas Day, New York, Volume 2, section 456, note c,[2]
quote.text: […]  in a plea to an action of debt on specialty, it is still necessary to show that the debt on which the judgment was recovered was a specialty, or to aver that the judgment was recovered before the defendant had notice of the plaintiff’s demand.
